change_description: Two identical replacements inside the file's embedded RLS SQL block: `user_id = auth.uid()` -> `user_id = (select auth.uid())` on the graph_nodes_user_isolation and graph_edges_user_isolation policies. This is the standard Postgres RLS initplan optimization (wrap auth.uid() in a scalar subselect so it is evaluated once per statement, not per row).
byte_accounting: `(select auth.uid())` is 9 bytes longer than `auth.uid()`; 2 occurrences x 9 = 18 bytes, exactly matching byte_delta. No other bytes differ.
root_cause: The file 24 content legitimately changed between v5.5.1 and v5.5.3 (two RLS-initplan optimizations, +18 bytes). It was NOT a corruption and NOT a CRLF/autocrlf artifact (both blobs contain zero CRLF). The discrepancy the v5.5.3 receipts flagged was that the MANIFEST/SHA256SUMS hash for file 24 was propagated forward from v5.5.1 (325355071ad4...) and did not follow the content change to 364380ff...; v5.5.3 recorded the true current hash for the first time. This receipt promotes the prior `unknown` status to `verified`.
correction_to_prior_receipts: ADR-20260719-01 and the v5.5.3 receipts described this as 'root cause unknown / out of scope' and only ruled out CRLF. With this direct blob diff the cause is now fully explained: a real, benign RLS optimization, with exact byte accounting.
method: git cat-file -p <blob> for both blobs; sha256 + byte + CRLF count computed on raw bytes; diff -u; occurrence count cross-checked.
